Il programma locale crea tabella e copie con riferimenti, senza consultare un database o inviare documenti a Mike; non anonimizza i dati.

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, verifies CPython 3.12 and its platform against both receipt and policy, and validates common recipes and enabled features independently of the initial launcher.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.

Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.

external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Lucia. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available.

external_boundaries.content: Unless the user requests --local-only, each substantive run with a durable local report automatically sends exactly schema version, one random per-run receipt UUID, the Lucia version when the request was first created, and the SHA-256 digest of the canonical local model-data report, plus ordinary connection metadata. controls: Vera report builds stamp by default. It does not change host model processing. Do not retry stamping without a later explicit user request. Service failures leave completed work and the local report intact and return pending. The generic Studio Archive helper also disables server attestation.

The client constructs a four-field allow-listed request, restricts production traffic to the fixed Mparanza HTTPS route, permits HTTP only on an explicit loopback port for testing, bounds responses, and rejects additional or mismatched response fields. The default transport rejects HTTP redirects before any redirected request and rejects endpoint URLs containing credentials.

The server rejects additional request fields, assigns its own timestamp, signs the complete retained record with Ed25519, stores only the minimal proof fields, applies request-size and rate limits, and fails closed when signing or verification keys are unavailable.

The local customer receipt states that the proof covers existence, server time, and report integrity only; it does not claim who submitted the digest, provider delivery, analytical correctness, semantic necessity, DPIA completion, legal advice, or GDPR compliance.

Retries retain the original UUID and version. A retry after finalization verifies the retained report against the sealed artifact manifest and writes supplementary receipts outside the immutable output tree.

The workflow remains subject to host network permissions and action-specific approval rules. A denied transmission is not retried through another tool or destination; permission-denied retries wait for the required authorization.

external_boundaries.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests remain unlinked until an actual native proof is received. Connector-owned runs can obtain the bounded per-run proof described above; run-specific computer bindings are used by counts and completion indicators. No personal account information or hardware identifier is collected. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product.
controls: Events are durably queued before transport and acknowledged by exact UUID, owner, sequence and hash. Interruptions stay outcome unknown; repeated submissions are idempotent.
Synthetic and agent-test runs are excluded from user metrics. Studio Archive is infrastructure and cannot be selected as a rated process.
The host AI selects the primary process and observes actual task completion. Counters and hashes do not assert professional correctness or independent model delivery.

The shared implementation binds registrations, OAuth resources, task events, report signatures, feedback and update downloads to one product. Existing unmapped installations and receipt schema 1 remain Vera. Physical-computer identity is shared, while usage catalogues and testing epochs are separated by product.

Authenticated event acknowledgements and run status expose the original owner's proven Computer ID and whether an actual signed receipt is linked. Missing linkage remains explicit and returns bounded follow-up instructions. Neither reporting gap changes the professional outcome or authorizes broader host access.

When local HTTPS is unavailable, the authenticated connector can stamp the exact retained receipt request for an owned run. The allow-list admits only receipt UUID, product/version, schema and report digest. It returns the same signed proof; a separate verified receipt event links it to the original run. No report or source contents are transmitted.

Connector-owned workflow acknowledgements return a random 15-minute proof scoped only to binding that original run to a native computer. The existing native helper adds its private computer capability and observed app. The server stores only the ticket hash, checks product, expiry and app, rejects re-binding, and never replaces the original owner or associates all runs from one saved connection with one computer. The proof cannot authorize other reporting operations. Exact event replay obtains a fresh proof without another event.

external_boundaries.purpose: Measure which user processes run and their observed outcome; link existing signed model-data receipts and technical reports without copying their professional content
external_boundaries.retention: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized. Host-link tickets expire after 15 minutes; their hashes and established run-to-computer bindings remain until administrative deletion. The raw short-lived proof is returned only in an authenticated acknowledgement and not in status or operator projections.

external_boundaries.content: The actual 1–5 integer score, up to 2000 characters of optional user-authored comment, source (chat or form), random event UUID and existing task binding. controls: The user supplies the score/comment for submission or clicks Invia valutazione; that action is the choice, with no second confirmation questionnaire.
